capabilities: Hide the window to the system tray when the close button is clicked
Toggle window visibility by clicking the tray icon
Quit Obsidian via the tray icon's right-click menu
disambiguation: Not a quick-note capture tool despite the tray icon; it explicitly offers no quick notes, hotkeys, or settings.
extras: Desktop only, single-window only, and tested on Windows 10/11; the README notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff and install is manual (download main.js and manifest.json).
intentEvidence: dragonwocky/obsidian-tray is great — but it's 500+ lines with a full settings UI.
motivation: The author wanted a single behavior — the close button minimizing to tray — without the 500+ lines and full settings UI of the existing obsidian-tray plugin.
problem: Obsidian's close button quits the app entirely, so users who want it to keep running in the background get no built-in minimize-to-tray option.

relations.evidence: Forked from dragonwocky/obsidian-tray via Piotr Adamczyk's fork
I wanted one thing: the close button should minimize to tray instead of quitting.

summary: Tray plugin that hides the Obsidian window to the system tray when you click close, with a tray icon to toggle and quit.
